Title: Tribunal says India cannot withdraw from water treaty with Pakistan
Article:
THE HAGUE: An international tribunal on Monday ordered India to "observe its obligations" under a treaty with Pakistan on the sharing of the Indus and other rivers, which the New Delhi government sought to suspend.
It also made an order "prohibiting" India from carrying out works at two hydro-electric projects that could breach the 1960 Indus Water Treaty.
The treaty governs the use of water from six rivers, whose headwaters originate in India but flow into Pakistan as part of the Indus basin – a resource relied on by hundreds of millions.
The Indus cuts through ultra-sensitive demarcation lines between India and Pakistan in contested, Muslim-majority Kashmir – a Himalayan territory both countries claim in full.
India said in May 2025 that it was suspending its membership of the treaty after accusing Islamabad of backing a deadly attack on tourists on the Indian side of Kashmir. Pakistan denied the charges.
India immediately rejected the Permanent Court of Arbitration's ruling that it had no grounds to withdraw from the treaty. Pakistan welcomed the tribunal's ruling.
India's Water Minister C.R. Patil said this year that the government would ensure that "not a single drop of water" will flow into Pakistan, which accused India of seeking to "weaponise" the precious resource.
Pakistan has previously said it would consider any attempt to change the flow of cross-border waterways as an "act of war."
The Permanent Court of Arbitration said in a statement that it had unanimously found that "none of the grounds" put forward by India to suspend the treaty were justified.
It said India's construction of hydro-electric projects on the Indus and associated rivers had to conform to the 1960 treaty.
"In a unanimous decision, the court found that none of these grounds could justify suspension or termination of the treaty," said a statement released by the panel.
"Accordingly, the Indus Waters Treaty remains fully in force, and India must observe its obligations under the treaty, including those relating to the design and operation of its hydro-electric projects on the Western Rivers," it added.

Title: Three killed, one injured after car plunges into five-metre-deep ravine
Article:
LAHAD DATU: Three men were killed while another was injured after the car they were travelling in skidded before plunging into a ravine along Jalan Hutan Simpan Bagahak here tonight.
The driver of the Proton Aeroback was believed to have lost control of the car while negotiating a bend, causing it to skid before plunging into a five-metre-deep ravine.
Lahad Datu Fire and Rescue Station chief Sumsoa Rashid said the department received an emergency call at 7.38pm.
He said firefighters who arrived at the scene found four men involved in the accident.
"Three victims were confirmed dead by Health Ministry personnel at the scene.
"The injured victim was taken to the hospital," he said in a statement.
He said the bodies of all the victims were handed over to the police.
"The identities of the victims have yet to be established and the operation ended at 8.45pm after the scene was confirmed safe," he said.

Title: Two killed, four injured in Mersing boat collision
Article:
MERSING: Two people were killed while four others were injured after two boats collided near Kuala Sungai Mersing tonight.
It is learnt that those killed in the incident were a boat skipper and a passenger who was a tourist.
The Fire and Rescue Department operations centre spokesman, quoted by Bernama, said the department received an emergency call about the incident at 9.04pm.
Following the call, a team of nine men from the Mersing Fire and Rescue Station was dispatched to Mersing jetty.
"When the team arrived, they found that a collision had occurred between two boats.
"Two victims were confirmed dead by medical personnel and handed over to the police for further action," the spokesman was quoted as saying in a statement to Bernama.
The spokesman also said four other victims who sustained injuries were receiving treatment, while the operation was still ongoing.
Meanwhile, Mersing district police chief Superintendent Abdul Razak Abdullah Sani, who confirmed the incident, said the case was still under investigation.
He also said police were expected to issue a statement on the collision soon.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Iran says 10 missing fishermen found in UAE
Article:
TEHERAN: Ten Iranian fishermen who went missing in Gulf waters weeks ago are alive in the United Arab Emirates and set to travel home soon, Iran's foreign ministry said on Monday.
Mohammad Soleimani, head of the ministry's representative office in Hormozgan province, said 13 fishermen had been missing since early August, amid concerns they may have been arrested after entering the territorial waters of neighbouring countries.
"Today, the UAE informed our embassy in Abu Dhabi that 10 of these fishermen are in the country and can leave from there," Soleimani said, according to the Iranian state broadcaster.
"Given that these individuals did not have their passports with them, the embassy of our country issued them travel documents, and they will return to Hormozgan on the first flight this week," he added.
There was no immediate response from the UAE on the report, and Soleimani added that "there is still no information about the other three missing fishermen."
"But we are continuing to follow up on their status in neighbouring countries," he said.
The development follows an announcement by Iran's embassy in the UAE in July that 55 detained Iranian fishermen had returned home following efforts by the embassy in Abu Dhabi and consulate in Dubai.
The latest returns come as the Strait of Hormuz remains a flashpoint in the conflict between Iran and the United States, with Teheran maintaining its closure of the strategic waterway and the two sides trading fire again on Monday after more than a month of relative calm.
Iranian media have also reported another case involving fishermen missing since May.
In August, IRNA reported that 17 fishermen from the southern port of Konarak, on the Sea of Oman, had been missing since May after their fishing boat, the Shahin 2, lost contact with other vessels when a US helicopter fired flares to disperse fishing boats about 70 nautical miles off Oman's coast.

Title: Man suffers burns as fire spreads to nine factory lots in Ipoh
Article:
IPOH: A man suffered burns to his body after a fire spread to nine factory lots in Persiaran Industri Bercham 10, Bercham, here this afternoon.
Perak Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said the 42-year-old man suffered burns to one per cent of his body in the incident and received first aid from emergency medical rescue services personnel at the scene.
He said 40 personnel and seven fire engines were deployed after the department received an emergency call at 3.36pm.
"The fire started at a Class B plastics factory measuring 30m by 13m, with 50 per cent of the premises affected.
"Other affected factories included Lots 10 and 11, which suffered 20 per cent damage; Lots 12, 13 and 14 (70 per cent); Lots 16 and 18 (80 per cent); Lot 15 (10 per cent); and Lot 17 (60 per cent)," he said in a statement today.
The fire was brought under control at about 6.25pm, and firefighters were conducting overhaul work, inspections and extinguishing residual fires to ensure there were no remaining sources of fire, he added.

Title: Iran war spurs Gulf investment in infrastructure
Article:
THE Iran war's redrawing of the global trade map is forcing Gulf nations to retool their investment playbook, ploughing capital into infrastructure — from energy pipelines to ports — to weather the fallout from the conflict.
The war has highlighted the Gulf's over-reliance on the Strait of Hormuz, previously a chokepoint for 20 per cent of global oil flows but also subject for decades to Iranian threats of disruption.
With the strait virtually blocked for much of the past six months, trade is being redirected to Saudi ports on the Red Sea and the United Arab Emirates' eastern ports, but capacity is smaller.
Gulf governments are looking at ways to create permanent, integrated solutions to get round using Hormuz, said an industry source.
While most Gulf governments can tap into oil riches accumulated over decades, some may look to external funds as they work towards ambitious foreign direct investment targets and as big infrastructure funds and other international investors show interest in the region's assets.
Ports have emerged as a "mission-critical priority" for Gulf governments, including Saudi Arabia, said a second industry source.
"If two years ago sports was the big buzz thing, I think for the time being, next year or two, they're going to say ports, ports, ports," he said of Saudi Arabia.
Abu Dhabi sovereign wealth fund L'IMAD said last week it plans to buy out the rest of AD Ports as it revamps the company's strategy.
AD Ports operates ports in the UAE and across the globe, but its UAE container throughput, as well as bulk and general cargo volumes, dropped by around two thirds in the second quarter from a year earlier as the company said it operated "through perhaps the most significant challenge in its 20-year history".
Dubai's DP World, one of the world's biggest port operators, also saw business decline in the first half.
It plans to develop two container terminals in Fujairah, where the UAE is building a new oil pipeline that will double crude capacity to Fujairah when it becomes operational next year. DP World is also working on inland container depots in the UAE.
Zin Bekkali, chief executive officer of UK-based investment management firm Silk Invest, said Gulf governments have the capital to fund some or most of this accelerated investment in infrastructure internally.
"So infrastructure is definitely an area which we think is going to benefit," Bekkali said.
Saudi Arabia has fast-tracked billion-dollar plans to steer oil away from Hormuz, sources said last month, potentially helping neighbours transport more oil without crossing the strait.
Beyond disruptions to shipping, strikes on production facilities in the Gulf have significantly affected oil refineries, aluminium plants and data centres among others, while air traffic remains below pre-war levels, impacting tourism and business flowing through the region.
On another level, the war has shaken the reputation of Gulf hubs as safe havens.
Qatar and Kuwait's economies are set to shrink by just over eight per cent this year, according to a Reuters poll, while Saudi Arabia's economy will expand by 1.4 per cent, after 4.5 per cent growth last year.
Qatar, one of the world's top liquefied natural gas (LNG) exporters before the Iran war, relies wholly on the strait to export LNG and also faces massive production shortages due to damage to its energy facilities.
There has been some opening up of Hormuz recently, but trade is limited and there is no clear end in sight to the conflict between Iran and the United States despite a cooling of hostilities.
Control of Hormuz is one of the most contentious points of disagreement, and countries are joining forces to find new ways to reduce reliance on it.
Turkiye and Saudi Arabia aim to build a railway to link the
two countries with Jordan and Syria in the next three or four years, Turkiye's transport minister said in June, adding that other Gulf countries would join the project.
"The recent Strait of Hormuz crisis has given us a very important lesson that these vulnerabilities are real... and they can happen anytime at any chokepoint," said Afaq Hussain, a former senior fellow at the Middle East Initiative at the Atlantic Council.
The writers are from Reuters
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Vietnam coffee farmers ride China's durian wave
Article:
VIETNAM'S  Central Highlands produces around one sixth of the world's coffee, but farmers are switching their traditional crop for durian to cash in on surging Chinese demand for the pungent "king of fruits".
"You can live okay with coffee, but it's durian that makes you rich," said Pham Xuan Lan, as he showed AFP journalists around his farm.
Blessed with a tropical climate and rich basalt soil, the lush Central Highlands produces vast quantities of robusta beans, and Vietnam trails only Brazil in coffee output.
But the area dedicated to durian has soared more than fivefold to 200,000 hectares nationwide over the past decade, according to the agriculture ministry.
Vietnam only officially entered the Chinese durian market after a 2022 trade protocol but last year became the country's biggest supplier by volume, ending Thailand's nearly two-decade dominance.
Lan was an early adopter, diversifying his crop two decades ago and now boasting 400 durian trees in Ea Knuec commune, part of Dak Lak province.
They produce 60 tonnes of the sweet yet smelly fruit, which is driven in frozen containers thousands of kilometres north into China.
The 56-year-old expects to make US$76,000 this year — against US$10,000 had he stayed with just coffee.
Other local farmers have followed suit, focusing on the premium Ri6, Musang King and Dona varieties.
During the August-October harvest, Dak Lak's roads are packed with trucks loaded with the spiky fruit, and at a durian festival this month, 525 vehicles formed what the Guinness World Records declared the largest-ever parade of fruit-carrying vehicles.
The boom is driven by demand from China, fuelled by a combination of expanding supply and growing popularity on social media, particularly among young people.
On Douyin, China's equivalent of TikTok, videos of users cracking open fruit with their bare hands have been watched billions of times.
"This tastes really sweet. It's almost like it's been coated in sugar," said Douyin influencer Liulianzi in a clip liked more than 17,000 times.
Once a luxury food, increased competition between Thailand and Vietnam and improved transport links have helped cut prices and make the fruit more affordable.
At a durian-tasting event in Beijing last month, Ada Song said  she had spent almost 1,000 yuan  on the fruit in recent weeks.
"I have tried nearly 20 different varieties," Song said.
Durian "tastes just as sweet as cake, without the greasiness and heaviness".
China imported almost US$7.5 billion worth of fresh durian last year, a nearly 12-fold rise from 2015.
Now Beijing is seeking to boost its homegrown produce, with more than 3,000 ha of plantations on the southern island province of Hainan, which has a similar climate to northern Vietnam.
But "our Hainan durians will
always be just a supplement to Southeast Asian durians", acknowledged Feng Xuejie, a durian expert at the Hainan Academy of Agricultural Sciences.
"It's not even a competition."
Vietnam's durian exports are expected to reach US$4 billion this year, up from US$180 million in 2021 — 90 per cent of them going to its northern neighbour.
But in the Central Highlands there are concerns about the reliance on China, as well as the risks of oversupply as more farmers join the rush.
Many anxiously eyed a recent price crash in Malaysia, blamed on an unusually bumper harvest.
Farmers warn durian is not a one-way bet, requiring a strict
mix of humidity, water and fertilisers.
Lan likened growing it to "raising a child —  I can give you all the tricks but I cannot guarantee you similar success".
He still grows coffee as his land is leased from a coffee company, allowing him to hedge his bets.
For some, the durian dream has already turned sour.
Hung, a farmer who gave only one name, switched entirely from coffee to durian five years ago, but switched back two years ago, admitting it was too hard to produce the quality required.
"I could not do it. I failed," the 42-year-old said. "So I would never go back to durian again."
The writers are from AFP

Title: Haze: Sarikei hits 303, bringing Sarawak's hazardous API areas to five
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Sarikei is the latest area in Sarawak to record a hazardous Air Pollutant Index (API) reading, bringing the number of areas in the state in the category to five as of 10.45pm today.
According to the Department of Environment's Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), Sarikei recorded an API reading of 303.
Serian recorded the highest API reading at 429, followed by Kuching at 385, Samarahan at 355 and Sri Aman at 342.
Sibu, Mukah and Samalaju were in the "very unhealthy" category, with readings of 266, 218 and 203 respectively.
Nine other stations recorded unhealthy readings, including Bintulu (189), ILP Miri (179), Miri (179), Kapit (171) and Limbang (162) in Sarawak.
Outside Sarawak, the stations recording unhealthy readings were Labuan (166), Kota Kinabalu (157), Kimanis (153), Keningau (152), Sungai Petani (151), Seberang Perai (131) and Seberang Jaya (112).
Meanwhile, 45 monitoring stations recorded moderate air quality, while Langkawi recorded the country's only "good" API reading at 45.
An API reading of between zero and 50 is categorised as good, 51 to 100 as moderate, 101 to 200 as unhealthy, 201 to 300 as very unhealthy, and above 300 as hazardous.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Iraq sentences kidnapper of US journalist to 15 years in prison
Article:
BAGHDAD: Iraq's judiciary has sentenced a man to 15 years in prison for the kidnapping of an American journalist who was abducted earlier this year by a powerful Iran-backed group, a judicial source said Monday.
At the height of the Middle East war, on March 31, Kataeb Hezbollah kidnapped journalist Shelly Kittleson in Baghdad, holding her for several days before setting her free just hours before the United States and Iran agreed to a ceasefire.
Iraqi authorities arrested one member of the group at the time.
According to a document shared by local media, a criminal court on Sunday sentenced Amir Rahim Jabbar to 15 years in prison under an "anti-terrorism law... for the crime of kidnapping" Kittleson.
A judicial source verified the document's authenticity to AFP, and a Kataeb Hezbollah source confirmed the ruling against one of its members.
Kittleson, who shared a copy of the ruling on X, said she was "grateful to the Iraqi judiciary".
Kataeb Hezbollah is among several pro-Iran armed groups that intervened in support of Tehran during the Middle East war, claiming attacks on US facilities in Iraq and across the region.
Under mounting US pressure to curb Tehran's influence, the new Iraqi government of Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi says it is committed to ensuring that pro-Iran armed groups, which Washington designates as terrorist organisations, hand over their weapons to the state.
The issue has fuelled tensions in Iraq, with several groups, including Kataeb Hezbollah, refusing to disarm.
Earlier this month, Kataeb Hezbollah accused Zaidi of engaging in "provocative and irresponsible actions".
Baghdad was once notorious for kidnappings and attempted abductions, but they have decreased as the security situation in Iraq improved in recent years.

Title: NST Leader: Subsidies are a lifeline, not a bottomless well
Article:
TODAY, the reinstatement of the Budi Madani RON95  (Budi95)  subsidy quota of 300 litres per Malaysian kicks in, a reprieve for citizens burdened by inflation.
Although the United States-Iran war is driving up   oil prices, the government made a difficult  decision: rather than deprive Malaysians of fuel subsidies, it will help absorb the costly  expenditure.
Budi95's bill  reached RM4 billion per month when oil prices jumped but Malaysians still paid a pump price of only RM1.99 per litre. This leaves precious little fiscal room to manoeuvre   as the reinstated quota requires  a delicate balancing act between cost-of-living pressures and subsidy reforms.
Malaysians must not view  the quota reinstatement as a sign   that the government's   financial position has become  stronger. Complex as it is, maintaining the   fuel subsidy is consistent with the nation's  commitment to  public welfare.
For decades, subsidised petrol has been so embedded in daily life that it  feels like an entitlement rather than a privilege.
When the government was forced to reduce the quota from 300 litres to 200 litres due to  a  spike in global oil prices, it  meant the government had less room to absorb subsidy costs.
Despite palpable pressure to cut public spending, the free to heavily-discounted healthcare, alongside cash aid for low-income households, singles and senior citizens, remain intact.  So do early schooling aid, transport discounts for seniors and persons with disabilities,  and various forms of  tax relief.
The bigger lesson is worthy of reflection: despite our many  problems, the government remains generous, always sensitive to citizens in need.   These measures reaffirm how blessed Malaysians feel to live in a country abundant in natural resources.
Despite being a developing economy, a wide social safety net   is available — a benefit not enjoyed even by some wealthier  countries. Still, none of these benefits should be taken for granted.
The temporary quota reduction serves as a reminder that public resources are not bottomless.  Subsidies do not magically  appear as   these are hard decisions,  funded by taxpayers.
At the same time, such  privileges  should not discourage constructive and legitimate scrutiny of government spending.
Malaysians have   the right to inquire whether subsidies are fairly distributed and whether public money is wisely spent. The lesson is  clear:  while remaining grateful, we must also acknowledge the need  to protect the country's fiscal position for future generations.
Following a string of  financial scandals, Malaysians must  exercise greater responsibility and willingness to protect public resources from leakage, abuse and wastage.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pakistan says welcomes Hague decision on water-sharing treaty with India
Article:
ISLAMABAD: Pakistan welcomed on Monday a decision by an international tribunal that a landmark water-sharing treaty remained in force, despite India's suspension of its participation.
"Pakistan welcomes this finding by the Court that interim measures are warranted," the government said in a statement following the decision by the Court of Arbitration in The Hague requiring India to pause work on a dam project.

Title: Nine secondary school students hurt in Sabah tour bus accident
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Nine secondary school students sustained minor injuries after the tour bus they were travelling in was involved in an accident at the Jalan Kota Belud-Kundasang T-junction today.
Kota Belud Fire and Rescue Station chief Elge Bakuk said the department received an emergency call about the incident at 11am.
He said the tour bus had been chartered to transport 35 students and a teacher from the school.
"The victims were transported in ambulances from the Health Ministry and Malaysian Civil Defence Force," he said.
The operation ended at 12.32pm, with no fatalities reported.

Title: At least 2,500 buildings destroyed in Nepal valley
Article:
PARIS: More than 2,500 buildings were destroyed in Nepal's Trishuli valley in tsunami-like glacial floods on August 26, according to an AFP computation of data from Europe's Copernicus observatory.
That's about two-thirds of all buildings in the three potentially affected zones studied by Copernicus' Emergency Management Service.
When partially damaged buildings are included, the proportion of structures affected rises to more than seven out of 10, underscoring the flood's violence as it tore through the valley.
These areas, which include parts of the towns of Timure, Syabrubesi and Bidur, north of the capital Kathmandu, were home to nearly 6,000 people before the disaster.
Images for the area around Bharatpur, Nepal's third most populous city, were still being studied on Monday morning.
Scientists attribute the flash flood to the collapse of a huge glacier in the Himalayas.
[[nid:1522987]]
It swept through the Gyirong border post between Nepal and Tibet, an autonomous region of China, after it raced some 20 kilometres (12 miles) down from the glacier.
The small border town of Timure and its surroundings lost more than 80 per cent of their buildings.
Ten kilometres further south, the disaster-stricken area of Syabrubesi lost nearly three-quarters of its buildings.
The village is the starting point for the famous Langtang trek and a route frequently used by Hindu pilgrims.
Further downstream, the riverbanks around Bidur – the administrative centre of the Nuwakot district and the base for the rescue teams – saw more than 1,800 buildings destroyed, or three out of every five.
As well as homes, the disaster destroyed roads and bridges, making it more difficult to deliver aid and search for the missing.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Lorry driver arrested with RM200k worth of ornamental plant saplings
Article:
RANTAU PANJANG: A lorry driver was arrested after 6,000 ornamental plant saplings worth RM200,000, believed to have been smuggled from Thailand, were seized at Kampung Padang Licin here today.
General Operations Force Southeast Brigade commander Senior Assistant Commissioner Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the seized plants comprised 2,000 frangipani, 2,000 cermai and 2,000 cactus plants.
"A GOF team from the Eighth Battalion stopped a lorry when it passed through the area about 11.30am.
"Checks on the lorry found the ornamental plants, which were believed to have been brought into the country illegally.
"A 61-year-old man who was driving the lorry was later arrested," he said.
He added that the suspect admitted to being involved in the activity for about five years and working for a Thai man.
"The suspect claimed that he was paid RM300 for each delivery of the plants to nurseries in Kedah," he said.
Radzi said the suspect and seized items had been handed over to the Agriculture Department for action under Section 5 of the Plant Quarantine Act 1976.
In another case, he said two men with eight previous criminal and drug-related records were detained with 33 litres of ketum juice in separate raids in Pasir Puteh yesterday.
Radzi said the suspects, aged 29 and 45, were arrested in Selising between 8pm and 8.45pm.
He said both suspects admitted to selling ketum juice for about a week as a source of additional income.
The cases are being investigated under Section 30(3) of the Poisons Act 1952 and Sections 15(1) and 12(2) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesia battles surge in forest fires as West Kalimantan hotspots nearly double
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesia is battling a sharp surge in forest and land fires in parts of Kalimantan, with hotspots in West Kalimantan nearly doubling to 7,377 on Monday.
National Disaster Mitigation Agency (BNPB) acting head of the Data, Information and Disaster Communication Centre Berton Panjaitan said the number of hotspots in West Kalimantan surged by 3,553 to 7,377, while fire spots rose by 88 to 104 and visibility fell to below one kilometre.
"In Central Kalimantan, hotspots declined by 147 to 5,244, but fire spots increased by 16 to 72, while in South Kalimantan, hotspots fell by 405 to 504, but fire spots rose by 33 to 55," he told an online press conference on Monday.
In Sumatra, Berton said hotspots in South Sumatra increased by 209 to 1,013, while they declined significantly in Riau and Jambi. The number of fire spots also decreased across the three provinces.
The fires are also taking a growing toll on public health, with nearly 5.5 million people living in affected areas across Sumatra and Kalimantan, Deputy Health Minister Prof Dante Saksono Harbuwono said.
He said about 13,500 acute respiratory infection (ISPA) cases were recorded cumulatively in July and August, with 4,082 people still suffering from ISPA as of Sunday.
"The health impact from the smoke this year is greater than last year," Dante said, adding that health authorities continued to monitor the situation and coordinate with local health offices.
Meanwhile, the Environment Ministry has flagged 42 companies for possible action over forest and land fires detected within their concession areas.
Environmental Law Enforcement deputy Rizal Irawan said the companies were identified by overlaying satellite hotspot data with concession maps, with 19 now undergoing field verification and the remainder to be inspected in a second stage.
"Regardless of whether it was deliberately burned or caught fire, when a fire occurs within a concession, strict liability applies.
"The company will be held accountable, either through administrative or civil sanctions," he told an online press conference.
Rizal said Indonesia was also coordinating with neighbouring countries over transboundary haze through Asean mechanisms, following a meeting of environment officials in Bali last month attended by ministers from Indonesia, Malaysia and Singapore.
On prevention efforts, Rizal said 95 Fire Care Community groups comprising 1,425 personnel had been established across six fire-prone provinces in Sumatra and Kalimantan, with another 35 groups planned this year.
He said notices were also sent to 2,226 companies last year requiring them to prepare personnel and facilities to prevent and respond to forest and land fires.
About 80 per cent had since reported their readiness, while the remainder had yet to respond.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesia raises 2027 subsidised fuel allocation, keeps LPG unchanged
Article:
JAKARTA:  Indonesia has raised the amount of diesel allocated to its subsidy programme in 2027, while keeping its liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) allocation unchanged, the energy ministry said on Monday in a parliamentary hearing.
Here are the details:
• Indonesia will allocate 19 million kilolitres of subsidised diesel in 2027, about 2 per cent higher than this year's allocation of 18.64 million kilolitres.
•  Energy ministry senior official Laode Sulaeman said at a separate meeting that subsidised diesel consumption this year is expected to reach 20.27 million kilolitres, exceeding the original allocation.
•  Indonesia has implemented a 50-50 blend of palm-based diesel and conventional diesel, known as B50 since the second half of this year in an effort to reduce its dependency on imported fuels.
•  The subsidised LPG allocation for next year is set at 8 million metric tons, unchanged from this year, but lower than the 8.67 million tons expected to be consumed this year.
•  Indonesia's oil lifting target has been set at 612,500 barrels of oil per day and 954,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day for 2027. — REUTERS
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: No automatic invitations to ex-PMs for National Day celebrations since 2018, says secretariat
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Former prime ministers have not been automatically invited to the National Day celebrations since 2018, the National Day 2026 secretariat said today.
Secretariat chairman Datuk Abdul Halim Hamzah said invitations for major official federal government events were managed by the Prime Minister's Department's Protocol and International Conference Secretariat Division.
"Based on the practice since 2018, invitations to the National Day celebrations are not automatically extended to former prime ministers.
"However, former leaders are not barred from attending and their attendance can be arranged through an application by the relevant party, in accordance with established procedures and the management of official invitations," he said in a statement today.
Halim, who is also communications ministry secretary-general, said the secretariat was informed by the Prime Minister's Office that former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad would be abroad from Aug 28 to 31.
He said the trip was based on an application for overseas rest facilities that had been received and approved by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, in accordance with provisions governing the remuneration and benefits of former prime ministers under the Members of Parliament (Remuneration) Act 1980.
Dr Mahathir, however,
made an appearance
at the 2026 National Day celebrations at Dataran Putrajaya here this morning.
In a live-streamed video on the TikTok account @chedetofficial, the 101-year-old statesman was seen waving to visitors while seated in an electric wheelchair.
The National Day celebrations drew thousands of Malaysians to Dataran Putrajaya.
Halim said the secretariat appreciated the attention and understanding of all parties.

Title: Anwar's 6 initiatives proof government listens to people, says Nga
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The six key initiatives announced by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim in his 2026 National Day Address yesterday take into account public feedback and the people's daily needs, Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming said.
He said the six initiatives would directly benefit the people, covering fuel subsidies, school maintenance, healthcare facilities, artificial intelligence (AI) training, e-Invoicing, as well as assistance for small traders and small and medium enterprises.
"The six initiatives announced by the Prime Minister are concrete proof that the Madani government listens to the pulse of the people and consistently prioritises their well-being.
"Malaysia's achievements over 69 years of independence would not have been possible without the shared contributions and efforts of all citizens, regardless of race, religion or background," he said in a statement today.
Nga said the spirit of unity and inclusivity should continue to be upheld to ensure Malaysia moved towards a more prosperous, fair and competitive future.
"Malaysia was built by Malays, Chinese, Indians, Dayaks, Kadazans and all citizens, regardless of race or background, working hand-in-hand to develop the nation," he said.
In his 2026 National Day Address, Anwar had announced
six additional initiatives

Title: 18-year-old college student dies after falling from 22nd-floor condominium
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: An 18-year-old private college student died after he fell from the 22nd floor of a residential premises in Setapak here this morning.
Wangsa Maju district police chief Assistant Commissioner Annas Sulaiman said the victim, a first-semester student at the college, was seen arriving at the premises at 7.07am.
He said the condominium had been converted into a hostel for students of the private college.
"At about 8.50am, police received a call from a security guard informing them of the incident," he said in a statement today.
He said the 18-year-old fell onto the sixth floor of the condominium and was pronounced dead at the scene by medical personnel.
He said the case had been classified as a sudden death report.

Title: For young PJ councillor, nation-building starts in his own 'kampung'
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: "I just want to make my corner of the country a little better," said Loh Y Lun, who hopes to be remembered simply as a Malaysian who rolled up his sleeves and served his community.
For the 26-year-old Petaling Jaya city councillor, that corner is SS2 — the neighbourhood where he grew up and now serves.
Taking up the role, Loh hopes to address everyday problems and improve services for residents.
"My main goal is to bring policy changes that have real benefits that people can feel," he told the New Straits Times.
Loh said the role was especially fulfilling because he was serving the city that shaped him.
"I know the ins and outs, I know what frustrates the residents, and I know what they need. It gives me the chance to directly improve my own 'kampung'."
However, becoming a councillor was not part of the plan.
[[nid:1522965]]
Loh, who holds a master's degree in public policy from Universiti Malaya, began his formal involvement in public service at 20 as an intern, although his interest in community work stretched back to his school years.
He later served as an assistant to a councillor and assemblyman before becoming a councillor himself in 2023.
"It was pure happenstance.
"It's definitely an unconventional path, and honestly wasn't something I actively sought out.
"If Covid-19 didn't happen, my career trajectory might have looked very different. But when the opportunity to serve came, I took it," he said.
His family initially had reservations.
With an undergraduate degree in finance, Loh said they had expected him to pursue a more conventional career in banking or the corporate sector.
Those reservations took a different turn as they later saw him settle into public service, particularly his grandfather.
[[nid:1522964]]
"My grandfather is my biggest supporter now.
"He cuts out my newspaper features, collects feedback from his friends who are local residents, and personally sends me complaints to look into.
"It makes him very happy whenever residents share positive feedback about me with him."
Away from council work, sport remains a big part of Loh's life, although his schedule now leaves him with less time for ultimate frisbee, volleyball and hiking.
He is president of the Malaysia Flying Disc Association and was involved in the Malaysian team that won one silver and two bronze medals at last year's SEA Games, where flying disc was a demonstration sport.
"It didn't count towards the official medal tally, but it was massive in the frisbee scene," he said.
Although his work is rooted in one part of Petaling Jaya, Loh sees it as part of a broader idea of what it means to serve Malaysia.
As the country marks its 69th National Day, he hopes Malaysians of his generation can build a stronger identity around what they share rather than the labels that separate them.
"When you go overseas, you don't actually say, 'I'm Malaysian Malay', 'I'm Malaysian Indian' or 'I'm Malaysian Chinese'. You just say, 'I'm Malaysian'," said Loh.
Nearing seven decades of independence, he believes Malaysians should ask whether they have grown closer to a common national identity.
"I want to be remembered as someone who tried to unite us, a sincere Malaysian who tried to make Malaysia more Malaysian than before," Loh said.

Title: Printed books remain a favourite despite rise of digital reading
Article:
KUCHING: In an increasingly digital world driven by constant screen exposure and e-readers, traditional printed books remain a preferred choice for readers seeking deeper cognitive engagement and a break from digital fatigue.
Despite the widespread availability of digital platforms, many readers maintain that physical books have a timeless appeal that electronic screens simply cannot replicate.
For Emily Abigail Richmond Allan, 30, choosing physical paperbacks over digital formats is a deliberate way of safeguarding her well-being while pursuing personal growth.
"After spending the whole day in front of a computer screen at the office, my eyes get tired, so at the end of the day, I just want to have some digital-free time at home.
"With physical books, there is a real sense of satisfaction. After finishing a book, there is that thrill of looking for another one.
"That is what keeps me coming back to traditional paperbacks and hardcovers," she said when met at the Big Bad Wolf Books Kuching event here today.
Her preference reflects a broader sentiment among avid readers, who view physical books not merely as static text, but as a deeply tactile experience.
Echoing this sentiment, Aiman Alfian, 29, also highlighted the hands-on benefits of printed books, particularly for early childhood education and managing screen time.
Looking towards his child's future, Aiman acknowledged that while online learning was sometimes unavoidable, printed materials should take priority whenever possible.
"If online learning is necessary, we don't have much choice. But if given the option, physical is definitely better.
"Children spend enough time looking at screens as it is, whereas physical books offer far better interaction," he said.
Similarly, mother-of-five Nurul Aien Ibrahim, 39, stressed the importance of physical books in supporting early childhood development and keeping young minds actively engaged.
"Physical books are crucial, especially colourful ones. Primary school children love vibrant colours, so I always buy physical books for them.
"It is quite rare for young children to enjoy reading online," said the Kelantanese, who has lived in Sarawak for nearly 15 years.

Title: Sri Lanka's ex-finance minister arrested over alleged corruption
Article:
COLOMBO: Sri Lanka's former finance minister Ravi Karunanayake was arrested on Monday for allegedly using state funds to pay his private employees, the country's main anti-corruption body said.
The former cabinet minister was taken into custody by the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) following a lengthy interrogation.
"The former minister was behind the payment of salaries to three people from the National Lotteries Board, but they did private work for him," a CIABOC official told AFP, requesting anonymity.
The arrest of Karunanayake, a member of former president Ranil Wickremesinghe's administration, comes amid a widespread crackdown on corruption by President Anura Kumara Dissanayake, who took office in 2024.
Another ex-minister, Keheliya Rambukwella, was arrested earlier this month for allegedly aiding the theft of a centuries-old sacred rock from the palace of the island's last Sinhala king.
Rambukwella was health minister when Sri Lanka faced an acute shortage of medicines after defaulting on its US$46 billion foreign debt in April 2022.
All the immediate family members of former president Mahinda Rajapaksa are also facing investigation or prosecution over money laundering, bribery and murder.
The Rajapaksas have denied all allegations.

Title: Sarawak sees rise in respiratory infection, conjunctivitis cases amid worsening air quality
Article:
KUCHING: Sarawak has recorded an increase in upper respiratory tract infection (URTI) and conjunctivitis cases amid deteriorating air quality since early August, with weekly URTI cases rising to 1,752 from about 1,717 at the beginning of the year.
Deputy Premier Datuk Dr Sim Kui Hian said the average number of conjunctivitis cases had also increased to about 21 a week, from 17 previously.
Dr Sim, who is also the state public health, housing and local government minister, said the increase in URTI cases was more pronounced in mid-August, particularly in several zones in Sarawak.
"The Southern Zone recorded about 1,250 cases, while the Central Zone recorded more than 1,000 cases and the Northern Zone recorded a peak of almost 400 cases," he said in a statement today.
He said the state Health Department was monitoring haze-related illnesses through 15 sentinel health facilities across the state.
The facilities focused on three main conditions associated with poor air quality, namely URTI, asthma and conjunctivitis.
From January to the end of August 2026, the sentinel health facilities recorded about 694,800 patient visits, including 64,688 URTI cases and 6,156 asthma cases.
Dr Sim said since the deterioration in air quality began in early August, health surveillance had shown a slight increase in URTI cases and a more significant increase in conjunctivitis cases, while overall asthma activity remained stable across Sarawak.
He said asthma cases presenting at the Emergency and Trauma Department of Sarawak General Hospital had also increased on several days throughout August, but overall monitoring did not indicate a sustained surge in asthma cases.
Meanwhile, Dr Sim gave an assurance that health facilities in Sarawak were adequately prepared to deal with any increase in haze-related cases, including in terms of medicine supplies and medical equipment.
Stocks of essential medicines and medical supplies, including three-ply masks, N95 masks and oxygen cylinders, were sufficient based on current usage.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Wanted man arrested after high-speed chase, second suspect on the run
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police arrested a 29-year-old wanted man after a 30-minute high-speed chase from the Awan Besar Toll Plaza to Salak Selatan today.
A second suspect in the same vehicle fled on foot and is being hunted by police.
City police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the incident occurred about 9.30am when Bukit Aman highway traffic police on patrol spotted a suspicious green four-wheel-drive vehicle near the toll plaza heading towards Klang.
He said police signalled the driver to stop, but he sped off, prompting a pursuit during which officers fired a shot at the vehicle's tyres.
"The chase is believed to have started at the Awan Besar Toll Plaza towards Klang and continued to Jalan Hang Tuah 4, Salak Selatan.
"The chase lasted about 30 minutes before the suspects' vehicle stopped near a petrol station in Sungai Besi.
"The suspect refused to cooperate and attempted to ram the police, prompting officers to fire five shots at the vehicle's rear right tyre," he said in a statement today.
Fadil said the suspect then fled towards Jalan Hang Tuah 4 before losing control of the vehicle and crashing into a grey Mazda.
He said police arrested the 29-year-old driver, while the second suspect escaped on foot.
"Checks of the vehicle uncovered tools believed to have been used to steal cables, as well as stolen cables.
"The suspect we arrested had 37 criminal cases and was also listed as a wanted person," he said.
The case is being investigated under Section 307 of the Penal Code, Section 42(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987, and Sections 427 and 379 of the Penal Code.
Section 307 carries a maximum prison sentence of 20 years upon conviction, while Section 42(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 carries a maximum five-year jail term and a fine of between RM5,000 and RM15,000.
Section 427 carries a jail term of between one and five years, a fine, or both, while Section 379 carries a maximum seven-year jail term, a fine, or both.
Fadil said police would apply for a remand order against the suspect under Section 117 of the Criminal Procedure Code tomorrow.
He said police were also tracking down the second suspect and urged anyone with information to contact the Brickfields police headquarters or the Brickfields police hotline at 03-2297 9222.

Title: Singapore to send humanitarian aid to Nepal for flood relief
Article:
SINGAPORE: Singapore will send humanitarian supplies and personnel to Nepal to support relief efforts following severe flash floods near the Nepal-China border, the Foreign Ministry said.
In a statement, the ministry said Singapore Police Force (SPF) officers specialising in Disaster Victim Identification (DVI) would be deployed at Nepal's request, while civilian and Singapore Armed Forces (SAF) supplies would also be delivered.
Foreign Minister Dr Vivian Balakrishnan conveyed the offer of assistance during a phone call with his Nepalese counterpart, Shisir Khanal, on Monday.
"In addition, the government will deliver humanitarian assistance comprising both civilian and Singapore Armed Forces (SAF) supplies to Nepal," the ministry said.
The latest assistance comes in addition to Singapore's US$100,000 (RM403,000) contribution on Friday to the Singapore Red Cross' (SRC) public fundraising appeal for relief efforts in Nepal.
To date, the SRC has raised about S$1 million (RM3.16 million).
The Foreign Ministry said its Crisis Response Team had been deployed to Nepal since Aug 27 to provide consular assistance to affected Singaporeans.
"The Singapore Government will continue to work closely with the Nepalese government on the provision of our humanitarian assistance," it added.
The death toll from devastating flash floods and mudslides along the Nepal-China border had risen to at least 919, while nearly 4,800 people remained missing, including 853 foreigners, authorities said on Monday, according to Anadolu Ajansi.

Title: HONOR X9e Pro smartphone makes first appearance at National Day Parade
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: HONOR has given Malaysians their first public look at the all-new HONOR X9e Pro, with the unreleased smartphone appearing in a striking purple finish at the National Day parade.
The device, which is set to launch in Malaysia soon, was worn by HONOR's humanoid robot at the parade before an audience of about 100,000 people.
The X9 series has established a strong presence in Malaysia's mid-range smartphone segment, with HONOR positioning it as a "national phone" for local consumers.
The company said the new X9e Pro would build on the series' existing strengths in durability and long battery life, while introducing a comprehensive upgrade.
The event also marked HONOR's first appearance at Malaysia's national-level National Day parade, with the company bringing its humanoid robot to the celebrations.
The appearance came less than a day after the robot made its debut at the Malaysia Marathon 2026, marking its first appearance outside China.
Its consecutive appearances at the two major Malaysian events saw the humanoid robot receive Asia Record and Asean Record certifications for being the "First Humanoid Robot to Complete a 10-Kilometre Public Road Run and March in a National Day Parade".
The recognition provided a formal record of the robot's unusual double appearance, which saw it move from the marathon route to the National Day parade within two days.
The choice of Malaysia as the humanoid robot's first overseas destination also underlines the importance of the local market to HONOR.

Title: Kuala Krai Market echoes with patriotic songs, traders wear Jalur Gemilang attire
Article:
KUALA KRAI: The atmosphere at Kuala Krai Market was different today when nearly 30 traders donned attire featuring the colours of the Jalur Gemilang, while patriotic songs rang out to enliven the National Day celebrations.
Bernama's survey found that the traders were not merely doing business as usual but took the opportunity to foster the spirit of love for the country by turning the market into a location to nurture patriotism among the community.
The red, white, blue and yellow colours of the Jalur Gemilang clearly brightened the market space, while the traders' unique appearance also attracted the attention of visitors who came to purchase their daily necessities.
Fish trader Mohd Redzuan Elias, 43, said the initiative undertaken proved that the spirit of patriotism could be fostered anywhere, including at daily gathering places for the community such as public markets.
"This year marks the sixth time we have celebrated National Day at the market by putting up the Jalur Gemilang and wearing clothes themed in the colours of the flag.
"Patriotic songs such as Bahtera Merdeka, Sejahtera Malaysia and Keranamu Malaysia were also played at this market to boost the spirit of us and the visitors who came," he said when met by Bernama today.
Grocery trader Noraini Mamat, 62, said the atmosphere not only brightened the surroundings of the market but could bring visitors closer to also appreciate the meaning of independence.
"When National Day comes, many visitors will come to the market with their families because it is a public holiday, so we traders take this opportunity by providing a unique attraction for them," said the trader who has been doing business at the market for almost 15 years.
Vegetable trader Ah Lin, 63, hoped more traders at other public markets would do the same to provide a special experience and allow the community to experience the National Day celebrations more closely.
Visitor Rosidah Mat Shah, 60, said the spirit of togetherness displayed by the traders at the market in conjunction with the National Day celebrations clearly demonstrated a symbol of love for the country. — BERNAMA

Title: Malaysia's rice self-sufficiency ratio needs to reach 80 per cent, says Mohamad
Article:
SERDANG: The country's rice self-sufficiency ratio (SSR) needs to be increased to at least 80 per cent to ensure supply remains at a comfortable level, Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu said.
He said his ministry would continue to strengthen the country's rice ecosystem and increase domestic rice production to ensure sufficient supply, as an SSR of below 60 per cent was inadequate for the country's food security.
"The efforts include encouraging companies and capable parties to open larger rice fields, with the cooperation of state governments in providing suitable land.
"We want to increase productivity and strengthen the supply chain by expanding the use of technology, encouraging innovation and opening up more opportunities for value creation throughout the industry chain," he said in his speech at a programme at Laman Padi in conjunction with the Malaysia Agriculture, Horticulture and Agrotourism Exhibition 2026 here today.
He said the agriculture sector was now developing through the use of data, technology, automation, artificial intelligence (AI), innovation and entrepreneurship, while also taking into account environmental sustainability.
However, he said these efforts needed to be accompanied by diligence and determination to ensure the targeted increase in productivity could be achieved.
In another development, Mohamad said his ministry wanted to explore an approach to integrating giant freshwater prawn farming with rice cultivation to produce two sources of yield from the same agricultural area.
He said he saw the potential of the approach during a visit to a rice-growing area where rice cultivation was integrated with giant freshwater prawn farming in China two weeks ago.
"In that rice field, there are giant freshwater prawns, so there are two yields, one from rice and one from prawns.
"The giant freshwater prawn fry were brought from Malaysia and breeding was carried out in China.
"We need to be more proactive in exploring the potential of integrating giant freshwater prawn farming with rice cultivation, considering that this approach has so far only been implemented on a small scale," he said.
Although Malaysia has more suitable weather conditions for giant freshwater prawn farming throughout the year compared with China, the potential to integrate such farming with rice cultivation has yet to be widely explored, he said.
He said the approach could be studied for future implementation, particularly in paddy areas with reliable irrigation systems, allowing the same area to be utilised for rice and giant freshwater prawn production.

Title: Budi Madani: Restored RON95 quota, higher diesel allocation bring relief to motorists, traders
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — The government’s decision to restore the assistance quota under the Budi Madani programme for RON95 petrol and increase the diesel quota has been well received by various layers of society and traders, considering it a timely step in alleviating the burden of living costs.
The announcement was made by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim during the 2026 National Day “Amanat Perdana” address at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre (PICC) yesterday.
In the address, he announced that the basic eligibility quota for RON95 petrol subsidies would be increased from 200 litres to 300 litres, while the Budi Diesel quota would be raised from 300 litres to 400 litres, effective today.
On average, beneficiaries stated that the return of the quota provided relief, especially in terms of monthly finances, and allowed expenses to be allocated to other basic needs.
Private sector worker, Furzani Ahmad, 24, said that the return of this quota contributed tremendously towards his commute to work.
For me, with this Budi 95, I can save a little on my monthly expenses. Almost every day, the distance I have to travel is almost 30 kilometres (km), so 300 litres is enough for a month, and sometimes there could even be surplus,” he said when met by Bernama.
Also sharing the same view, Darwisy Khairudin, 23, was happy with the government’s decision to restore the Budi 95 quota.
“The distance from my workplace to my home is only about 20 km to 25 km, but sometimes I have outside assignments, so I have to calculate whether the fuel quota is enough or not. Therefore, it’s really good that the government has reinstated this quota,” Darwisy said.
Meanwhile, fruit stall operator Abdul Manan, 63, who uses a diesel vehicle to transport his supplies, described the increase in the Budi Diesel quota as helping to stabilise his daily operating costs.
He said that the return of the quota reduces the burden of logistics expenses, thereby allowing him to maintain reasonable fruit prices for customers.
“Sometimes we take stocks from far away, so the petrol consumption is definitely high. Therefore the increase in the diesel quota at least provides relief to our working capital so that the selling price does not need to be raised,” he said.
The Budi Madani programme is a government initiative to ensure that fuel subsidies are distributed in a targeted manner. — Bernama

Title: College student dies after fall from Setapak condominium
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — An 18-year-old college student died after falling from the 22nd floor of a condominium in Setapak here this morning.
Free Malaysia Today reported that Wangsa Maju police chief Annas Sulaiman said police were alerted at about 8.50am after a security guard found the student’s body at Residensi Teratai on Jalan Langkawi.
The victim, a first-semester student at Universiti Geomatika Malaysia, had returned to the university-provided condominium unit at about 7.07am, according to CCTV footage reviewed by police.
Annas said the footage showed the student subsequently falling from a corridor on the 22nd floor to the sixth floor.
“The victim was confirmed dead at the scene. The case has been classified as sudden death and further investigations are being held to complete the probe,” he said in a statement.
